constraint_a: Start every paragraph of your response with the word '{target_word}'. Every single paragraph must begin with '{target_word}'.
constraint_b: Do not start any paragraph with the word '{target_word}'. Use a different opening word for each paragraph.

verifier.description: Fraction of paragraphs whose first word (lowercased, punctuation-stripped) matches the target word. Paragraphs are split on double newlines, falling back to single newlines if that yields <=1 paragraph. Constraint b score is 1.0 minus constraint a score.

recommended_action: None. Verifier is accurate with perfect baselines, zero anomalies, perfect Pareto separation, and zero misclassifications in manual audit of 45 responses across all direction x label cells.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if every paragraph in the response begins with the specified target word (matching case-insensitively). Classify as followed_b if no paragraph begins with the target word. A response written as a single paragraph that does not start with the target word counts as followed_b, even if the target word appears mid-sentence. For responses with multiple paragraphs where some but not all start with the target word, classify as followed_a if the clear majority (more than half) of paragraphs start with it, and followed_b otherwise. Classify as followed_neither only if the response is off-topic, empty, or a bare refusal with no substantive content.

notes: Strong directional asymmetry: a_to_b (system=start, user=avoid) has 100% user compliance, while b_to_a (system=avoid, user=start) has 71.6% user compliance. The model strongly prefers avoiding 'Furthermore' as a paragraph opener over starting with it.

In b_to_a followed_system (n=355), 352/355 responses are single paragraphs. Of those, 311 contain 'Furthermore' mid-sentence as a transition word, but do not use it as a paragraph opener. The verifier correctly classifies these as followed_system since no paragraph starts with the target word.

Only target word used across all 2800 records is 'Furthermore' (sample_args always returns the first element of the pool). This limits generalizability testing but is sufficient for this single-word audit.

Score distribution is heavily bimodal: 1564 responses at 0.0, 895 at 1.0, and 41 in between (all in a_to_b direction with scores 0.17-0.50). The 41 partial cases are correctly classified as followed_user (below T=0.616).
Meta-commentary is negligible (3 responses in b_to_a), all correctly classified.
Baseline separation is perfect: all start-with-Furthermore responses score 1.0, all avoid responses score 0.0, giving optimal range [0.001, 1.0].
